Question: How in the world did the US Supreme Court decide that the US government does not have the right to ban bump stocks? Democrats, Republicans, Trump, the NRA, and more than 80% of all Americans supported banning bump stocks!
Old_Answer: I don’t think the NRA’s “endorsement” of regulation of bump stocks was much more than an attempt to thwart further gun regulation. Kind of a thing where they say “we don’t want you messing with anything else, so we’ll give you this one”. It was a knee jerk reaction to the mass killing in Las Vegas in 2017. They knew they had little ground to stand on there. As for the Supreme Court decision, it’s only slightly quizzical, given the makeup of the court. But the scope of the question was narrow. The window they were looking through was small - does the bump stock in and of itself make a weapon automatic; meaning does the weapon itself change characteristics. And the answer to that is no. The bump stock is an individual object. It cannot on its own be considered automatic weaponry, despite it’s singular use. The bump stock uses a semi automatic weapon’s recoil to allow the gun to fired in rapid succession. What it doesn’t do is allow a single pull of the trigger to fire off multiple shots - the recoil of the bump stock bounces the weapon allowing multiple pulls in rapid succession. Yep, that’s it - the question that was asked of the Supreme Court was probably the wrong one, and they gave the only possible answer. I’d also be willing to bet the question posed to the Court was set up that way by the NRA. They would not want to make the bump stock manufacturers upset, and they knew how to work around their own words. So the decision of the SC, despite it’s ridiculousness, was the correct answer given the question asked and our definition of automatic weapons. The government can ban automatic weapons, but it can’t ban a device used to make a weapon automatic unless the specific function of that device is to make multiple shots fire rapidly with one pull of the trigger. It doesn’t matter that the reality is you only depress your finger one time and the bump stock does the rest, apparently.
